subject: Learning Methods
title: Sketchnoting
description: A fast breakdown of Sketchnoting for builders.

hook.text: Sketchnoting: effective learning usually works differently from what feels easiest.

buildup.text: Sketchnotes combine simple drawings, icons, and text to capture ideas visually. Artistic skill is not required.

discovery.text: Sketchnoting reveals the principle that makes the learning stick.

twist.text: Sketchnoting shows that effective learning often feels harder in the moment.

climax.text: Start with five basic shapes: circles, squares, arrows, stars, people. These cover most visual note-taking needs.

punchline.text: Draw simple icons. Your memory doesn't need art. It needs visuals.

quiz.question: Why do sketchnotes improve memory compared to text-only notes?
options: Drawing takes longer so you spend more time with the material
Combining visual and verbal processing creates dual coding
Colored pens are more engaging than black ink
